item.title: A 1,256-megawatt nuclear reactor on Lake Erie accidentally became a wildlife sanctuary, now spotted turtles nest inside its buffer zone
item.description: Over the last two centuries, Ohio has witnessed a drastic decline in wetlands, significantly affecting wildlife habitats. However, the land preserved around a nuclear power plant serves as an essential sanctuary for endangered spotted turtles. These turtles thrive in shallow waters rich in vegetation, and the plant's ongoing operations offer a critical generational opportunity for their survival. This unexpected refuge demonstrates nature's remarkable ability to endure amidst human expansion.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1908, Eliza Homans donated 140 acres of land to stop future development, six years later it became a part of Acadia National Park
item.description: Eliza Homans made a remarkable contribution of 140 acres to establish Acadia National Park, incorporating breathtaking locations like the Bowl and the Beehive. This generous act marked the first significant donation to the Hancock County Trustees of Public Reservation, laying the groundwork for the park's creation. In recognition of her impact, Homans Path was later integrated into the park's expansive trail system, ensuring her legacy persists within its natural beauty.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Streamer Nitro_Camden’s Twitch stream takes an unexpected turn after StableRonaldo sends 15,000 viewers
item.description: Nitro_Camden, a Twitch streamer, saw his viewer count skyrocket following a raid. However, the celebration was short-lived when his mother barged in, frustrated with the noise, and unplugged his gaming gear. The unexpected showdown became a viral sensation on social media, emphasizing the unpredictable dynamics of live streaming and the impact of personal life on online popularity.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: UAE is turning desert sand into eco-friendly bricks, the method cuts cement needed for construction to nearly half
item.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers have engineered eco-friendly bricks using desert sand and various industrial by-products. These bricks boast enhanced sulfate resistance when compared to traditional cement options. An innovative curing process at room temperature minimizes energy use, offering a sustainable alternative to Portland cement. However, further industrial evaluations are essential for these bricks to gain traction in the market.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1962, 5 Swans escaped a Maryland estate; 40 years later, about 4,000 threatened the Bay
item.description: Five mute swans escaped from an estate in Maryland in 1962 and their descendants multiplied to nearly 4,000 in the Chesapeake Bay region within four decades. The invasive birds eat large amounts of underwater grasses and have also been linked to the displacement of native birds, raising concerns among wildlife managers about their growing impact on the Bay's ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 19-year-old Canadian student's invention helps people with cerebral palsy paint and write; sold in 25+ countries
item.description: Lianna Genovese, a Canadian student, has created an inspiring device called Guided Hands to assist children with cerebral palsy in expressing their creativity through painting. This innovative tool harnesses arm and shoulder movements, enabling young artists to engage with touch screens effectively. Originally composed of basic materials, Guided Hands has transformed into a recognized commercial assistive technology, earning accolades worldwide for its significant impact.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: N Korea fires 10 missiles amid US scaling back military drills with the South
item.description: On Thursday, North Korea fired ten short-range ballistic missiles into eastern waters, a provocative move following the United States' decision to reduce joint military exercises with South Korea. The South Korean military enhanced its monitoring efforts and shared intelligence with its allies. Meanwhile, North Korea dismissed diplomatic outreach from the US President as unworthy of a response. Such missile tests violate United Nations Security Council resolutions.

item.title: 16-year-old girl runs onto field to tackle player and protect brother during game — watch
item.description: A 16-year-old Tennessee girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after authorities said she ran onto a football field during a middle school game and tackled a player involved in a scuffle. The game was ended early, and the girl was later released to her parents. She has also been banned from school properties for life and from Cornersville Middle School athletic events for one year.

item.title: Iowa family moves a $12,000 farmhouse four miles on wheels for dream home
item.description: An adventurous Iowa family took on the challenge of rescuing an abandoned farmhouse they believed held untold stories. By moving the century-old building four miles to their land, they endeavored to preserve history while crafting their dream home. Faced with surprising renovations and repair costs, they shared their transformative journey online, earning a global audience and ultimately building a unique family haven that mingled modern life with historical charm.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US scientists are building a $12 million 'digital brain' for drones inspired by insects
item.description: At Penn State, a research team is pioneering advanced drone decision-making systems modeled after insect neural mechanisms. Utilizing analogue computing alongside graphene materials, this initiative focuses on onboard data processing that replicates the natural filtering and coincidence detection seen in biology. With annual demonstrations of evolving prototypes, the goal is to enable fully autonomous drone swarms independent of external support.
